Staffing software is a platform that runs a staffing agency’s recruiting, client, and placement work in one place. Some tools cover the front office and back office together. Others cover one layer, such as screening, and connect to your system of record. The best one depends on your placement type and your slowest step. This guide compares 9 tools, shows which stack layers each covers, and explains how to choose, what it costs, and how to switch.

## What is staffing software?


Staffing software is the system a staffing agency uses to win clients, fill job orders, place workers, and get paid. It tracks candidates and clients, receives orders from vendor management systems, and handles timesheets, payroll, and billing. A general ATS covers only candidates and jobs for one employer.


It is one part of the wider market for[recruiting software](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/best-recruiting-software-of-2025/) , built for agencies that bill clients. Staffing tools usually span four layers:


- **Front office:** ATS and[recruitment CRM software](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/recruitment-crm-software-2025/) for candidates, clients, and job orders
- **Screening and interviewing:** first-round screens before a recruiter calls
- **Middle office:** VMS connections, onboarding, and compliance forms
- **Back office:** time entry, payroll, and client billing


**What staffing software is not:**


- A shift scheduling or workforce management tool
- A staffing marketplace that supplies workers
- An RPO service (software for RPO firms overlaps in places, but this guide focuses on agencies that bill clients)

## How did we evaluate staffing software?


Every tool was reviewed under the same criteria, with data dated November 2026. No vendor paid for placement. Peoplebox.ai publishes this guide and is listed first by editorial decision. The order is not a ranking or a score. Every entry lists limitations.


### Data sources


- **Vendor pages:** product, platform, and pricing pages, read in November 2026
- **G2:** ratings, pricing tabs, and review themes, with contact-sales tools labeled
- **Peoplebox.ai research team:** independent review of pages, features, and content depth across all 9 tools


### Selection framework


1. **Built for agencies:** the vendor’s own pages name staffing or recruitment agencies as buyers
2. **Covers a layer end to end:** at least one stack layer is built in, not only integrated
3. **Has a live product page:** current product and pricing information is public or on G2
4. **Has a G2 profile with reviews:** so readers can check ratings themselves

## How should a staffing agency choose software?


A staffing agency should choose software by fixing its slowest step first, then checking how each layer connects. List where recruiters lose time, which client programs run through VMSs, and how pay and billing work today. Then test 2 or 3 tools against that list.


- Look for a[recruitment automation software](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/best-recruitment-automation-software/) that holds candidates, clients, and job orders, so recruiters stop retyping data.
- Look for VMS connections that bring job orders in without email or copy and paste.
- Look for a[candidate screening software](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/candidate-screening-software/) that reaches every applicant before a recruiter calls, by phone, text, or video.
- Look for redeployment tools that flag workers whose assignments end soon.
- Look for time entry, payroll, and billing that share pay and bill rates with the placement record.
- Look for[recruiting funnel metrics](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/recruitment-metrics/) reports on time to submit and fill rate.
- Look for full data export, so leaving later does not cost your candidate history

## How much does staffing software cost?


Staffing company software cost depends on seats, modules, and connections. Most tools charge per user or per recruiter each month. Back office modules, VMS connectors, and AI features are often quoted separately. Setup and data migration can add one-time fees. Ask for the full annual price before comparing tools.


Cost driver What to ask


Seats Is pricing per user, per recruiter, or per branch?


Modules Are payroll, billing, and onboarding in the base price?


VMS connectors Is each VMS connection priced separately?


AI features Are AI screening or interviews priced by seat, credit, or interview?


Setup Is there a one-time setup or training fee?


Migration Who moves candidates, clients, and placement history, and at what price?


Contract What is the minimum term, and what happens to data at the end?


## How do you switch staffing software without losing candidates or placements?


You switch staffing software safely by moving data in stages and running both systems for a short overlap. Export everything first, keep pay and bill history readable, reconnect VMS and job board feeds, and test at 2 or 3 branch locations before every recruiter moves over.


1. Export candidates, contacts, clients, job orders, placements, notes, and documents
2. Keep the old system read-only until the current year’s payroll records are closed
3. Map pay rates, bill rates, and assignment dates before importing
4. Reconnect each VMS feed and job board account, and check one live order end to end
5. Run both systems through one full pay cycle
6. Train two power users per branch first, then the rest of the recruiters
7. Pilot at 2 or 3 branch locations, then roll out to the rest


## Which staffing software is right for your agency?


The best staffing agency software is the one that covers your agency’s weakest layer without breaking the others. Temp and light industrial agencies usually need a full front and back office suite. Contract firms need timesheets tied to billing. Agencies already on a good ATS often need faster screening more than a new system.


Start with the problem, not the vendor list. Fix the slowest step first, then test 2 or 3 tools at 2 or 3 branch locations for 30 days. If screening is the slowest step, see how[Peoplebox.ai runs first-round interviews](https://www.peoplebox.ai/ai-interview-software/) .


## FAQs


### 1. What software do staffing agencies use?


Most staffing agencies run an ATS and CRM as their system of record, a VMS connection for client programs, and a back office tool for payroll and billing. Many also add an AI screening layer.


### 2. Is there free staffing software?


Yes. Zoho Recruit has a free edition for one recruiter. Manatal starts at $15 per user per month billed annually. Agencies running payroll, billing, or VMS feeds will likely need a paid plan.


### 3. What is the difference between staffing software and an ATS?


An ATS tracks candidates for open jobs. Staffing software also tracks clients, job orders, placements, timesheets, and pay and bill rates. In-house hiring teams with no clients to bill usually compare[applicant tracking systems](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/best-applicant-tracking-systems/) instead.


### 4. Can an AI interviewer work with Bullhorn?


Yes. Bullhorn sells AI screening through its Amplify digital workers. Separate AI interviewers, including Peoplebox.ai, connect to Bullhorn, interview applicants, and write scores back to the candidate record. Confirm the sync during a demo.


### 5. Is AI interviewing legal for staffing agencies in New York City?


Yes, with conditions.[NYC Local Law 144](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/businesses/faq-automated-employment-decision-tools.page) covers employers and employment agencies that use automated employment decision tools. It requires a yearly bias audit and notice to candidates. This is not legal advice; ask counsel.


### 6. What are signs your staffing software is holding recruiters back?


Recruiters retype data between systems, applicants wait days for a first call, VMS orders arrive by email, and timesheets need spreadsheet fixes. Two or more of these signs usually mean a stack layer is missing.
